title: Shortest and Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
summary: Given a binary string and a positive integer k, find the shortest beautiful substring with exactly k ones.
statement: Given a binary string and a positive integer k, find the shortest beautiful substring with exactly k ones. If no such substring exists, return an empty string. A substring is beautiful if it contains exactly k ones. The output should be the lexicographically smallest among all shortest beautiful substrings.
constraints: s is a nonempty binary string and k is positive.
A beautiful substring contains exactly k ones.
Return the shortest beautiful substring, breaking length ties lexicographically; return an empty string if none exists.
hints: For exactly k ones, leading zeros only make a candidate longer.
Use a sliding window with at most k ones, trim leading zeros at equality, and compare candidates by (length,string).
Shrink past excess ones; when the count is k, remove left zeros and update the best tuple.
Every shortest k-one interval begins and ends with one, and the scan reaches that canonical interval for each right endpoint; tuple comparison enforces both objectives.
editorial: Every shortest k-one interval begins and ends with one, and the scan reaches that canonical interval for each right endpoint; tuple comparison enforces both objectives.
